chapter: Rhythm Club, studio dates and the 1930s big bands
title: The clean life of band musicians
summary: The pay was modest but the life was clean; players in top bands had to live like gentlemen, with little drug use.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: -- (inaudible) of musicians. All the money wasn't great, but the life was great.
The life was clean. Your family -- you could raise your family. We didn't have everything, you know.
We had our bad years and the lean years and everything. But the guys didn't turn to dope and stuff like that.

There was a few reefers around, but nothing, you know.
To get in a band like Fletcher Henderson or Chick Webb or -- Teddy Hill had a good band -- or another band -- young guy with a great band, you know -- from the time that Teddy Wilson had his band.
You get into those bands, not only you had to be a musician, but you had to be a gentleman. You had to live clean. They didn't just (inaudible) take you in there.
